note.question: What determines the supply chain contract design problem faced by a data-driven supplier (she) who needs to respond to the inventory decisions of the downstream retailer (he)?
note.overview: The rise of big data analytics has automated the decision-making of companies and increased supply chain agility. In this paper, we study the supply chain contract design problem faced by a data-driven supplier (she) who needs to respond to the inventory decisions of the downstream retailer (he). Both the supplier and the retailer are uncertain about the market demand and need to learn about it sequentially over a fixed time horizon.

In this case, even if the supplier does know the market demand (yet the retailer still does not know it), inferring the retailer’s inventory learning policy from his ordering decisions is still a difficult task.
Now the supplier cannot directly infer the retailer’s ordering decisions in each period without knowing the retailer’s observations and inventory learning policy.
That is, the retailer makes inventory decisions as a function of the supplier’s wholesale prices, the observed demand realizations, and his particular inventory learning policy.
